text: Metformin is recommended as first-line therapy for Type 2 Diabetes in patients with CKD when eGFR >= 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. In patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (CKD Stage 4 and Stage 5), Metformin is strictly contraindicated due to the high risk of fatal lactic acidosis. Insulin or alternative therapies should be considered.

topic: Blood Pressure Management in Advanced CKD
text: While ACE inhibitors and ARBs provide renal protection in proteinuric CKD Stages 1-3, initiating or escalating high-dose ACE inhibitors (e.g., Lisinopril) in advanced CKD Stages 4-5 carries severe risks of hyperkalaemia and acute declines in GFR. Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (such as Amlodipine) are preferred for blood pressure reduction in advanced renal failure when RAAS blockade cannot be safely monitored.

source: ADA 2024 Standards of Care in Diabetes
text: Insulin therapy (basal or basal-bolus regimens) remains the gold-standard and universally safe pharmacological intervention for glycaemic management in advanced renal impairment (CKD Stages 4-5), as it does not rely on renal tubular clearance mechanisms that provoke lactic acidosis.

Primary first-line agents for hypertension in the general adult population include thiazide diuretics, calcium channel blockers (CCBs), and ACE inhibitors or ARBs. For initial monotherapy in uncomplicated hypertension without renal contraindications, any of these classes is acceptable.

topic: Evaluation and Staging of Chronic Kidney Disease
text: Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 4 is clinically classified by sustained eGFR between 15 and 29 mL/min/1.73 m2 (severely decreased). Stage 5 kidney failure is classified by eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m2. Advanced CKD Stages 4-5 mandate immediate renal safety reviews and contraindication flags for nephrotoxic and renally cleared drugs.

source: ADA 2024 Standards of Care in Diabetes
topic: Diagnostic Criteria and Initial Management for Type 2 Diabetes
text: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is clinically diagnosed by an HbA1c >= 6.5%, fasting plasma glucose >= 126 mg/dL, or clinical documentation of persistent hyperglycemia. In patients with preserved eGFR >= 60, Metformin is first-line monotherapy; in severe renal decline (eGFR < 30), Metformin is withheld and Insulin is initiated.

Stage 2 Essential Hypertension is clinically defined as systolic blood pressure >= 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >= 90 mmHg. In patients without advanced renal impairment, ACE inhibitors (Lisinopril) or CCBs (Amlodipine) provide effective blood pressure control. When advanced CKD coexists, calcium channel blockers avoid hyperkalaemic and acute hemodynamic risks.
